claims.statement: The AI Act requires providers of high-risk systems to document post-market monitoring that actively collects and analyzes lifecycle performance data.
The Commission lists risk management, data quality, logging, documentation, human oversight, robustness, cybersecurity, and accuracy among high-risk AI obligations.

contrary_evidence: Cloud vendors, governance suites, and quality consultancies already offer broad AI compliance tooling, while implementation timelines remain changeable.

economics.acquisition_route: One-to-many distribution through cybersecurity insurers, AI quality consultancies, and conformity-assessment partners.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 250 vendors at 2500 PLN blended monthly revenue yields 7.5 million PLN ARR by year five and can support founder equity above 5 million PLN without double-counting retained earnings.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 3-4 founder hours daily on evidence automation while external counsel owns legal classification.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 80-88% gross margin after storage, test compute, reviewer escalation, and channel share.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: a 7000 PLN partner integration pays back after three release packs.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis, including the capital figure: 2500 PLN per model-release pack plus 1900 PLN monthly evidence retention and monitoring.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Every release, substantial modification, periodic audit, and serious incident produces another evidence event.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Permissioned failure-taxonomy and remediation outcomes improve test selection without exposing customer models
fingerprint.customer: Small EU providers of potentially high-risk AI systems
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embedded workflow distributed by insurers, AI quality firms, and assessment partners
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Model lineage, evaluation, logging, and monitoring evidence sold per release and subscription
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The AI provider pays when a version-bound evidence pack is signed and retained
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A model version is released, materially changed, audited, or implicated in an incident

founder_fit: AI governance evidence is technically aligned, capital-light, repeatable, and distributable without a personal brand.
risks: The service cannot promise conformity and must keep classifications, legal advice, and final approvals with qualified parties.

structure.control_point: The immutable link among model version, evaluation evidence, logs, approval, and post-market plan
structure.critical_dependency: Correct scope classification and acceptance by auditors, insurers, or notified bodies

thesis: Embed a signed model-version evidence gate with AI quality consultancies and insurers, charging on every release, substantial modification, and incident while pooling anonymized evaluation-failure patterns under explicit rights.
title: ModelRelease AI Evidence Gate
uncertainties: It is unknown whether channel partners value shared failure benchmarks enough to grant derivative-data rights.
